title: Incident Certification & Evidence Authorship Protocol
author: Avery Chen
body:
Summary:
This protocol standardizes how SREs certify incidents, author and validate evidence artifacts, and reconcile SLO/error-budget impacts. It ties incident-level evidence to capacity planning and long-running reliability initiatives so action items are auditable, machine-parseable, and repeatable.

Scope:
- Applies to all incidents where a declared SLO breach occurred or where the error budget burn rate exceeded 3x sustained for a 1-hour window.
- Includes incidents with customer-facing impact, internal availability regressions, and high-latency events affecting production inference.
- Out of scope: trivial alerts with no SLO/error-budget impact (e.g., short-lived resource spikes < 1 min with no page).

Definitions:
- Certification: formal sign-off that an incident has complete evidence, causal analysis, and a remediation plan.
- Evidence artifact: any telemetry snapshot, trace, profile, replay, config diff, or runbook excerpt attached to an incident.
- Authorship: the act of assembling, annotating, and validating evidence; the author is accountable for artifact quality.
- SRE EVI Tool: internal CLI/automation that validates evidence schema and uploads signed artifacts to the incident tracker (see Automated tooling).

Principles:
- Evidence-first: every certified incident must contain reproducible telemetry and at least one actionable hypothesis trace.
- Machine-parseable artifacts: artifacts should follow the evidence JSON schema to enable automated audits and SLO reconciliation.
- Ownership clarity: authorship and certification steps are explicit in the incident record.
- Link to capacity: incidents that consume error budget trigger a capacity remediation assessment within 48 hours.

When to initiate certification:
1) Post-incident when severity >= Sev2 (customer-visible partial outage) or when SLO breach detected.
2) When error budget burn rate > 3x sustained for 1 hour.
3) After any multi-region failover or cross-cluster degradation.

Certification workflow (high level):
1. Triage owner creates incident stub and sets "certification_required": true.
2. Author assembles evidence artifacts and runs automated evidence lint via SRE EVI.
3. Runbooks and remediation playbook are attached; capacity assessment performed.
4. Senior SRE reviewer performs evidence review and either certifies or remands for more artifacts.
5. Upon certification, incident is marked "certified" and queued for SLO reconciliation and capacity planning.

Required evidence artifacts (minimum):
- One end-to-end trace showing request path and error or latency hotspot (trace ID and span snippet).
- Telemetry snapshot (Prometheus metrics/resolution >= 1m) covering -30m to +60m around incident start.
- CPU/GPU memory heap profile or allocation snapshot for affected runtime (if applicable).
- Deployment and config diffs (git commit SHAs) for any releases in the incident window.
- Canary and synthetic check results that indicate pre-incident drift (if available).
- Post-incident remediation PR or rollback link.

Evidence quality checklist (author must confirm):
- Artifacts include timestamps (ISO 8601) and timezone.
- Traces contain sampling decisions and full span tree to the service boundary.
- Metrics are labeled with tenant/service identifiers.
- If sampling prevents a full trace, include synthetic replay that reproduces the failure.

Automated tooling and commands:
- SRE EVI (evidence linter and uploader)
  - Install: pip install sre-evi (internal package)
  - Basic validation: sre-evi validate --incident 2026-1302 --evidence ./artifacts
  - Upload & sign: sre-evi upload --incident 2026-1302 --author achen --sign
  - Example success output:
    {status: OK, issues: 0, uploaded: 6, signed: true}

Evidence JSON schema (minimal example, used by tooling):
Note: double quotes in the example are required by the validator. When constructing artifacts use the schema exactly.

{
  "incident_id": "2026-1302",
  "artifact_type": "trace",
  "timestamp": "2026-02-09T14:23:00Z",
  "author": "achen",
  "service": "inference-router",
  "tags": ["sev2", "slo-breach"],
  "reference": {"trace_id": "abcd1234efgh", "collector": "jaeger-prod"}
}

(Automated tooling will reject submissions missing incident_id, timestamp, or author.)

Certification review criteria (senior SRE):
- Completeness: all required artifacts present and pass SRE EVI lint.
- Causality: at least one credible causal chain is documented (not necessarily final root cause).
- Remediation: short-term remediation and long-term action items identified and assigned.
- Accountability: authorship attributed and reviewer recorded.

SLO & error budget reconciliation (upon certification):
1. Trigger: incident marked "certified".
2. Automation queries SLO ledger for affected service(s) and computes episode impact (tokens/requests lost, availability windows).
3. If incident consumed > 10% of monthly error budget for the service, schedule an immediate capacity and model-serving review within 48 hours.
4. If burn rate > 5x, apply the emergency capacity hedging runbook (see Capacity planning handoff).

Capacity planning handoff (within 48 hours of certification if threshold met):
- Deliverables from SRE author to capacity planners:
  - Incident impact summary (table below)
  - Peak concurrent requests delta and P95 latency uplift
  - Evidence artifacts (links to signed artifacts)
  - Suggested short-term hedges (e.g., increase dedicated pool by N GPUs, enable model-variant fallback)

Incident impact summary (example table):
- Service: inference-router
- Window: 2026-02-09T14:12Z to 2026-02-09T15:05Z
- P95 latency pre: 220ms; during: 580ms; post: 230ms
- Availability impact: 99.86% for the month -> projected monthly delta -0.06%
- Error budget consumed (estimated): 18% of monthly budget

Capacity remediation options (short list):
1) Increase dedicated pool by 2x for 12 hours (fastest, costly).
2) Enable quantized model variant for <10% degraded quality, reduces GPU memory and latency.
3) Route a percentage of low-priority tokens to best-effort pool (no SLA).

Post-certification actions and tracking:
- Create a ticket in Reliability Initiatives backlog with label "slo-mitigation" and link to certified incident.
- Assign action items: remediation owner (P0 within 72 hours), long-term capacity change (P1 within 30 days).
- Add to monthly SLO review board agenda if incident consumed > 5% of monthly error budget.

Runbook excerpt: "SLO Reconciliation and Capacity Hedging" (triggered after certification):
1. Run automation: curl -s "https://internal-api.redwood/slo/ledger?service=inference-router&window=2026-02-09T14:00Z,2026-02-09T16:00Z" > impact.json
2. Inspect impact.json and verify error_budget_consumed > threshold.
3. If threshold exceeded, open capacity request via Terraform change request: tf plan -var 'gpu_pool=dedicated-heap-4' && tf apply -auto-approve.
4. Notify stakeholders: #sre-oncall, #infra-capacity with summary and artifact links.

Retention and evidence governance table:
- Artifact type: Traces -> Retention: 90 days -> Access: SRE + Debugging tier
- Metrics snapshots -> Retention: 365 days -> Access: Platform + Product
- Heap/profile dumps -> Retention: 180 days (encrypted at rest) -> Access: SRE + Security on approval
- Deployment diffs -> Retention: 5 years -> Access: Platform + Compliance

Ownership and roles:
- Triage owner: first responder, creates incident stub and assigns author.
- Evidence author: assembles and uploads artifacts, responsible for initial hypothesis and validation.
- Senior SRE reviewer: certifies artifacts and approves incident certification.
- Capacity owner: reviews and schedules remediation/hedge.
- Reliability program lead: ensures long-term initiatives are created and tracked.

Escalation matrix (certification blockers):
- Missing telemetry: contact observability team within 4h.
- Encrypted artifacts inaccessible: contact security and provide signed request.
- Disagreement on causality: escalate to Reliability program lead for arbitration within 24h.

Metrics to track protocol adoption:
- % of certified incidents with complete evidence on first submission (target >= 85%).
- Median time from incident close to certification (target <= 72h).
- % of certified incidents that trigger capacity review and result in a mitigation within 30 days (target >= 70%).

Appendix A — Example evidence upload session:
$ sre-evi validate --incident 2026-1302 --evidence ./artifacts
Validation results: 0 errors, 1 warning (missing synthetic replay)
$ sre-evi upload --incident 2026-1302 --author achen --sign
Upload complete: https://incidents.redwood/2026-1302/artifacts

Appendix B — Quick certification checklist (for reviewer):
- [ ] Evidence lint: pass
- [ ] Trace attached with causal path
- [ ] Metrics window covers pre/during/post
- [ ] Remediation PR/rollback link present
- [ ] Capacity handoff created if required
